bib.title: Chapter 4: Building a Web Scraping Agent with an LLM (in Building AI Agents with LLMs, RAG, and Knowledge Graphs)

question: How is an LLM turned into an agent (brain, perception, action), how are agents and planning strategies classified, which libraries build them, and how does one build a simple web-search agent?

A web-search agent with LangChain tools and zero-shot ReAct

limits: No experiment or benchmark; Figs 4.3 and 4.4 (speed and GPT-4-judged quality of LLMs) are described without model names, sizes or scores in the text.
Library comparison is qualitative and dated to LangChain v0.2; the code uses the legacy initialize_agent with agent='zero-shot-react-description'.
The 'web scraping' title is broader than the content: the code only wraps search tools (DuckDuckGo, Serper, Wikipedia), no HTML scraping code.
Chapter says memory is covered in the next chapter; agent here has nowhere to save information.
practices: Choose the agent LLM by closed vs open source, parameter count against cost, infrastructure cost, and domain knowledge (fine-tune or retrieval) (Brain section).
Benchmark candidate LLMs on tokens per second and tokens per second per billion parameters, and judge answer quality with a larger model such as GPT-4 (Brain section, Figs 4.3-4.4).
Plan in two stages, formulation then reflection, with the plan checked by the LLM or a second model (Brain section).
Prefer decomposition-first for overview and fewer hallucinations, interleaved decomposition when errors must be corrected (Classifying AI agents).
Use RAG for agent memory when retrieval is accurate, fine-tuning when experience should be internalised at higher cost (Classifying AI agents).
Pick the framework by language, task, community, customisation: LlamaIndex for retrieval, Haystack for Q&A, LangChain for broad scope, Semantic Kernel for .NET (Choosing an LLM agent framework).
Keep the sources a search agent used so answers can be backtracked, because generative search can hallucinate (Creating an agent to search the web).
Give each LangChain tool a name and a description so the LLM knows when to use it (Creating an agent to search the web).

terms.definition: an artificial entity that perceives its surrounding environment via a set of sensors, makes a decision, and implements it
three-part framework: brain integrates, stores and decides; perception extends input modalities; action uses tools to modify surroundings
The LLM divides the task into a series of subgoals and solves them sequentially
Task decomposition and planning are interleaved
several different plans are generated for each task, then the best is chosen (majority vote, tree search or RL)
use of an external memory system to enhance the agent's decision-making and planning capabilities
also called the instructor-executor paradigm: humans provide instructions via natural language and agents execute
an equal partnership between the agent and the human
